If the static gate passes, stop this action without claiming functional correctness and hand off only the now-unblocked case_vcs_functional_sim followed by case_vcs_evidence_analyzer as the next current-layer verification decision.

executable_actions.rationale: The current causally earliest blocker is the exact-board identity and canonical VCS compile-plan binding failure. A bounded repair of the generated manifest/compile-plan provenance is required before the current-layer real VCS run can be trusted or before any lifecycle-frontier trace can localize hardware. This action preserves the exact wrapper and all semantic contracts, and intentionally excludes connected-kernel replay and RTL changes.

observations: The earliest executed current-layer failure is real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface, not a localized RTL failure: the board simulation manifest does not bind the current board identity, compile authority, ordered-command Vivado-export contexts, or authorized simulator executables.

Because case_axi_ddr_interface failed, case_vcs_functional_sim and case_vcs_evidence_analyzer are dependency-skipped in the current verification run. Consequently no fresh exact-board functional, numeric, data-order, AXI/DDR, lifecycle, or full weight-consumption claim can be made.

The older board progress artifact reports full core ingress with ready core egress and zero output, but contract_guided_debug_closure classifies the present blocker as verification_capability_gap. This artifact is debug/planning evidence only while the exact compile-plan identity gate is failed; it cannot justify an RTL root-cause decision or a lower-layer backtrack.

The connected-kernel capability is hash-bound closed evidence: the targeted replay observed complete 1792-beat ingress and egress with terminal last, 416 accepted trace records, and boundary liveness pass. No new valid current board trace names a certified-invariant contradiction.

The lower-layer certificates remain reusable read-only. Their elastic variable-latency semantics require boundary order and cross-token overlap, not same-cycle completion across unequal-latency stages.

All 17 active scoped contamination barriers and open retry requests 0136, 0140-0144 remain active. They prohibit downstream promotion and treating rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts as validated inputs; this candidate repair does not clear them.
The conditional design-team review returned no_split, so there is no specialist result that can substitute for the failed deterministic board binding evidence.
proposed_actions: Repair the generated exact-board simulation-manifest/compile-plan producer so it derives, rather than hardcodes, source_identity_sha256, selected source-closure hash, compute-slot ABI hash, Vivado export facts, per-command authority references, and authorized executable provenance from the existing exact board identity. Hash-check preservation of immutable board and semantic artifacts, then rerun only the failed case_axi_ddr_interface gate. Do not run VCS functional simulation, analyze a board frontier, modify RTL, or reopen the connected kernel in this action.
risks: Board-fact risk: altering or simplifying the user-supplied wrapper, its source closure, compute-slot ABI, or Vivado facts would invalidate exact-board evidence. The repair must update only generated compile-plan/provenance binding metadata.

Implementation/runtime risk: an unbound compile plan may compile a different source closure or invoke an unauthorized executable, so stale output-frontier, AXI, DDR, prefetch, and loader observations cannot establish the selected DUT behavior.

Model/shape/numeric/data-order risk: until a fresh exact-board run completes, the immutable target-model expected outputs, resolved tolerance, semantic-testbench contract, tensor shape/order, and output ordering are not re-established at board scope.

Memory/weight risk: existing tensor hashes and historical loader/prefetch progress do not prove that the DUT in a newly authorized board compilation consumed all required Transformer-block tensors. That proof is deferred to the unblocked board functional run.

SACG trust risk: promotion, backend synthesis, implementation, bitstream generation, runtime-ABI release, and board runtime remain blocked; no active barrier may be cleared merely because the manifest rebinding candidate is generated.
Lower-layer contamination risk: rerunning the connected-kernel replay before a valid current board contradiction would waste certified evidence and violate the hierarchical repair loop.

constraints: Use the exact user-supplied board wrapper and immutable source-closure, compute-slot ABI, Vivado-facts, semantic-testbench, checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, and numeric-policy hashes.
Bind every VCS compile-plan command and executable to the current exact board identity and cited Vivado export/tool-profile authority; do not guess tool names or replace the wrapper.
Treat active contamination barriers and retry requests as downstream-consumption and promotion blockers until a fresh Stage7 result passes.
Do not reopen operator leaves or the connected kernel without a new current hash-bound board trace explicitly contradicting a named lower-layer invariant.
Do not change tolerance, golden outputs, target reference, checkpoint, stimulus, tensor scope, or Transformer-block DUT boundary.
edges: certified single_transformer_layer_kernel evidence -> board integration debugging (read-only reuse)

output.summary: Fail closed at the board_axi_ddr_wrapped_system layer. The next causally distinct action is to repair and hash-rebind the generated exact-board VCS compile-authority/identity manifest, then rerun only case_axi_ddr_interface. The current functional VCS/analyzer results remain blocked by that failed static gate; therefore the recorded output-frontier stall is not currently promotable hardware evidence. The certified connected-kernel targeted replay is closed and must not be rerun or repaired.
